Actions: Search for monitoring-location URLsFind all waterdata.usgs.gov referencesFind HOOVER references in web/Find parameterCode=00060 in app.jsFind popup formatting functionsFind formatPortalHtml functionSearch HOOVER in fetch_water_data.pySearch waterdata in telemetry.html +15 more

Root Cause & Resolution: 400 Bad Request on USBR-HOOVER

#### 1. Why Did the 400 Server Error Happen?

  • USGS WaterData URL Constraint: The USGS National Water Information System (waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/<ID>/) strictly expects numeric 8- to 15-digit USGS site identification codes (such as 09380000 for Lees Ferry or 09095500 for Cameo).

  • The Telemetry ID Switch: When we standardized and deduplicated the facilities database, we canonicalized the Lower Colorado Dam hydroelectric releases to their true operational authority: USBR-HOOVER, USBR-DAVIS, and USBR-PARKER (because USGS retired its physical in-river gaging stations below those dams decades ago, and the Bureau of Reclamation Lower Colorado River Operations meters and publishes them directly).

  • The Hardcoded Fallback Bug: In [web/app.js](file:///Users/macstudio/Documents/Antigravity/CO_River/web/app.js#L4526), the map station popup formatter (formatGaugePopup) was hardcoding:

javascript
  <a href="https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/${s.id}/#parameterCode=00060">#${s.id} ↗</a>

When clicking on the Hoover Dam Release streamflow marker, it dynamically generated https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USBR-HOOVER/#parameterCode=00060. Because USBR-HOOVER is a string ID, USGS rejected the request with HTTP 400 Bad Request: Invalid site number.

---

#### 2. The Fix
1. Dynamic Authoritative Portal Routing ([web/app.js](file:///Users/macstudio/Documents/Antigravity/CO_River/web/app.js)):

  • Connected formatGaugePopup and openReachPopup to the system's getPortalInfo() helper.

  • For USBR-HOOVER, USBR-DAVIS, and USBR-PARKER, station links now route directly to the official USBR Lower Colorado River Operations Hourly Teletype:

[https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/hourly.html](https://www.usbr.gov/lc/region/g4000/hourly/hourly.html)
  • Colorado DWR diversion tunnels (ADATUNCO, MOFTUNCO, ROBTUNCO, BOUTUNCO) route to the CDSS Surface Water Portal:

https://dwr.state.co.us/Tools/Stations?station=<ID>
  • Standard 8-digit numeric streamgages route to https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/<ID>/#parameterCode=00060.


2. Accurate Provider Badges & Code Snippets:
  • Popups for USBR-HOOVER now display a distinct emerald badge: USBR Dam Release (rather than mislabeling it as a USGS Gage).

  • The API / Python tab now renders authentic Python code scraping the USBR RiverOps hourly teletype table with the USBR teletype endpoint URL, eliminating invalid queries against the USGS NWIS REST API.


3. Fallback Hardening Across the Platform ([web/sankey.html](file:///Users/macstudio/Documents/Antigravity/CO_River/web/sankey.html#L1531) & [web/test_proposal1.html](file:///Users/macstudio/Documents/Antigravity/CO_River/web/test_proposal1.html#L1378)):
  • Hardened all node card link formatters: non-numeric string IDs now check /^\d{8}$/ before attempting to construct a waterdata.usgs.gov URL, automatically falling back to USBR or CDSS.


---

#### 3. Verification

  • Verified live rendering and link routing via automated Chrome DevTools Protocol:

Actions: Search for sidebar-link CSS in index.htmlMeasure link dimensions and positions on clickSearch academic-top-header in index.htmlTrack frame by frame movement on tab clickRun debug nav click scriptRun multi-tab switch testCheck computed styles of active vs inactive linkSearch for sidebar-link focus CSS +6 more

The 1-pixel repositioning and readjustment on click has been eliminated:

1. Root Cause

1. Asymmetrical Border Thickness: Inactive links had border: 1px solid transparent, while active links had border: 1.5px solid var(--hairline). This created a 1px physical height discrepancy between inactive and active states. 2. Transitioning Layout Properties: transition: all 0.15s ease animated the border thickness and padding across state toggles, causing the element to expand over 150ms and push all neighboring buttons down by a pixel before settling. 3. Fractional Padding: padding: 6.5px 10px introduced half-pixel subpixel anti-aliasing jumps on font glyph calculations. 4. Unscoped Iframe Focus: Switching to the Map tab called iframe.focus() without { preventScroll: true }, allowing the browser to trigger a micro-scroll.

---

2. Engineering Fix (web/index.html, web/editorial.css, web/style.css)

  • Strict Geometric Invariance: Inactive links now have permanent border: 1.5px solid transparent !important and border-left: 3.5px solid transparent !important. The .active state strictly overrides border-color and border-left-color without changing border thickness ($\Delta h = 0.00\text{px}$).
  • Integer Pixel Padding & Line-Height: Replaced padding: 6.5px with crisp integer pixels (padding: 6px 10px !important), explicit line-height: 1.25 !important, box-sizing: border-box !important, and outline: none !important.
  • Targeted Transitions: Restricted transitions strictly to color properties: transition: background-color 0.12s ease, border-color 0.12s ease, color 0.12s ease !important (never layout dimensions).
  • Gutter & Scroll Protection: Applied scrollbar-gutter: stable to .sidebar-academic and passed { preventScroll: true } to all iframe.focus() calls.
---

Verification

  • Automated CDP Test: Verified computed dimensions across all tab switches — every button remains identically invariant at 30.00px whether active or inactive, with $\Delta = 0.00\text{px}$ movement.

Here is a concrete, two-track cleanup plan. Each phase is self-contained so we can execute and visually verify one pass at a time without breaking working functionality.

---

Track 1: UI & Information Architecture Cleanup

Phase 1 — Navigation & Window Consistency (Eliminate Modal Jank)

Right now the left navigation bar mixes three different behaviors: in-panel tabs (Overview, System Map, Water Budget, Architecture & Methodology), pop-up modal overlays (Law of the River, Data Sources), and external links (GitHub Repository ↗).
  • Convert Law of the River and Data Sources from pop-up modals into standard in-panel tabs (just like Architecture & Methodology).
  • Eliminates the awkward double-close pattern (both an ✕ at top-right and a Close / Close Legal Review button at the bottom of modals).
  • Keeps the left navigation bar visible at all times and gives long-form reading (5 legal chapters, compact tables, API dictionaries) the full viewport height instead of a cramped scrolling box.
  • Remove redundant in-page navigation:
  • In [sankey.html](file:///Users/macstudio/Documents/Antigravity/CO_River/web/sankey.html): remove the bottom #budget-data-sources card, the top Data Sources & Legal Authorities ↓ button, the footer jump link, and the bottom-right ← Back to Inflows & Consumptive Depletions link on View 2.
  • In [telemetry.html](file:///Users/macstudio/Documents/Antigravity/CO_River/web/telemetry.html): audit the Schema & Dictionary modal for duplicate close buttons (keep only the top-right ✕).

AI-generated layouts default to wrapping every small group of facts in nested boxes ("cards inside cards"), which wastes margins and shrinks body text down to 10px–11px.

Actions: Locate reservoir stacked area chart in index.html

You're spotting a real rendering bug plus a color-palette clash in [index.html](file:///Users/macstudio/Documents/Antigravity/CO_River/web/index.html#L2289-L2338):

1. Muddy alpha-blending bug (fill: true): In Chart.js, fill: true fills every layer all the way down to y = 0 instead of stopping at the layer below it (fill: '-1'). Because all three layers are semi-transparent (0.30–0.35 alpha), Lake Powell (amber) is being painted on top of Lake Mead (blue), turning the middle band into muddy olive-khaki, and Upper CRSP (green) is painted over both, turning the bottom band into swamp green.
2. Clashing categorical colors on large areas: The chart uses bright Okabe-Ito categorical hues (blue, mustard amber, emerald green) plus a heavy black 2.5px top line and a red dashed threshold. Those work for small scatter points, not large stacked area blocks.
3. Heavy competing outlines: Every band has its own thick 1.75–2.0px colored stroke fighting the 2.5px charcoal total line.

Two clean ways to fix it

1. Stepped river-blue stacked area (recommended): Fix the stacking (fill: '-1' so layers never bleed into each other), replace the blue/amber/green clash with a cohesive 3-step muted river-blue/slate palette (e.g., deep river blue #2b5c8f for Lake Mead, muted steel blue #6c93b8 for Lake Powell, pale mist #b8cddf for Upper CRSP) with thin 1px crisp dividers and a subtle top line. 2. Clean line chart (no big solid fills): Drop the stacked fills altogether and plot Combined Total, Lake Mead, Lake Powell, and Upper CRSP as crisp lines with only a very faint tint under Combined Total.

Which direction do you prefer?

1. Section 1 — Architecture & Dimensional Framework:

2. Section 2 — Geospatial River Network & Dynamic Shoreline Rule (folded from 01):
  • Inspect web/data/river_network.json topological DAG (26 reaches, dam splits, trans-basin tunnels) and demonstrate the Cataract Canyon dynamic re-emergence threshold against Lake Powell's pool elevation.

3. Section 3 — Live USGS/USBR Telemetry & Mainstem Reach Mass-Balance (folded from 02):
  • Live USGS NWIS / USBR API ingestion + sequential mainstem reach gain/loss table (cfs).

4. Section 4 — Relational Database Architecture & SQL Analytics (sqlite3, from 04 + Capstone):
  • Normalized schema (stations, reservoirs, annual_lees_ferry, rbi_flashiness) and analytical SQL views (view_system_storage_summary, view_compact_surplus_deficit, 10-year rolling Compact compliance).

5. Section 5 — The 104-Year "Wet Water" Ledger & Reservoir Buffer Depletion (from 03 + 04 + Capstone):
  • Figure 1: 1922 Compact Allocation Paradox (1922–2026 natural flow vs. 15.0/16.5 MAF statutory claims & cumulative deficit).

  • Figure 2: Major Reservoir Storage Capacity vs. Active Volume depletion bar chart.

6. Section 6 — Tributary Dynamics: Travel Times, $K$-Means Regimes & Flashiness (folded from 03 + 04):
  • Figure 3: Empirical Cross-Correlation (CCF) Hydraulic Travel Time to Lake Powell (1.5 to 8 days).

  • Figure 4: Richards-Baker Flashiness Index ($RBI$) & Unsupervised $K$-Means ($k=4$) hydrograph regime separation.

  • Volumetric Proof: Flash flood spike (10,000 cfs for 6 hrs = 4,959 AF) vs. sustained alpine snowmelt (15,000 cfs for 60 days = 1,785,124 AF, 360× more volume).

7. Section 7 — Production Export Contract & Conclusions:
  • Demonstrate how SQLite + ingestion scripts compile the static JSON contracts consumed by the serverless web dashboard.
